items.subject: Grocery: semantic sweep found 7 product(s) no rule can see - 2026-09-18
evidence: RE-MEASURED 2026-09-20: audit-semantic-identity.ps1 run live, exit 0, SEMANTIC-IDENTITY-COMPLETE. 'examined 2629 shipped pair(s) and 8676 rule-invisible product(s) in 1.5s on cuda'. COVERAGE: 8 product(s) across 6 commodities.

THE ROOT FIX IS WORKING. The same run printed 'semantic-identity: 13 finding(s) suppressed as EXCLUDED (a rule saw and refused them; explain-coverage-gap lists them)' and 'semantic-identity: 1 coverage finding(s) suppressed as TRUNCATION ARTEFACTS'. 14 of 22 findings suppressed by the classifier 37ac63 shipped; on 2026-09-18 that suppression did not exist and every one of them would have paged.
explain-coverage-gap.ps1 over today's findings: 'explained 21 coverage finding(s): EXCLUDED 11, NO-INCLUDE 8, REFUSED-BY-EXCLUDE 2'.

THE 8 NO-INCLUDE, adjudicated one by one. FOUR ARE CORRECT REFUSALS (a different product): cooked-jasmine-rice | Baker's | 'Ben's Original Ready Rice Cilantro Lime Flavored Rice' and | 'Ben's Original Ready Rice Roasted Chicken Flavored Rice' (the commodity's include requires the word jasmine; these are not jasmine); laundry-detergent | Family Fare | 'Arm & Hammer Detergent, Clean Meadow 100.5 Fl Oz' (the commodity is Arm & Hammer OxiClean / Odor Blasters specifically); wild-rice | Walmart | 'Wild Black Rice by Gerbs - 2 LBS' (black rice is a different grain).

FOUR ARE REAL PRODUCTS OF THEIR COMMODITY that the include is simply too narrow to see: feminine-pads | Walmart and | Baker's | 'Stayfree Classic Pads ... Super Long' (the include knows maxi/feminine/overnight/always/ultra-thin pads, not 'Classic Pads'); maple-syrup | Baker's | 'Pearl Milling Company Syrup Original' (the include HAS an 'original syrup' pattern and the store wrote the words in the other order); onion-soup-mix | Walmart | 'Lipton Recipe Secrets Onion Dry Recipe Soup and Dip Mix' (the include needs 'onion recipe soup' adjacent and the store put 'Dry' between them).

AND THE WIDENING BUYS NOTHING TODAY, measured by the estate's own gated tool. apply-coverage-batch.ps1 -WhatIfOnly over those three patterns: 'crown changes: 0'; feminine-pads 6 -> 6 cells, maple-syrup 5 -> 5, onion-soup-mix 3 -> 3; 'value: +0 cell(s), -0 cell(s), 0 commodit(y/ies) got a cheaper real price'; reveals 2, 3 and 2 previously-invisible rows; 'theft check: OK'. Each admitted product is DEARER than the cell its own store already holds: 0.1818/each vs Baker's 0.1408, 0.1663/floz vs Baker's 0.0912, 0.9358/oz vs Walmart's 0.49 crown.

THE GATE THEN REFUSED THE BATCH and reverted it: 'tile-integrity failed: 2 hard fault(s) on BATCH commodities, 223 pre-existing elsewhere' -> 'unrepaired: feminine-pads [Sam's Club] PRICE-DRIFT', 'unrepaired: feminine-pads [Fareway] PRICE-DRIFT' -> 'REVERTED: audit-tile-integrity: 2 batch commodit(y/ies) still disagree with their tile after repair - this is the cheese collision shape', exit 2. commodities.json verified byte-identical to HEAD afterwards.

THE CLASS 37ac63 LEFT OPEN HAS NOW HAPPENED. Its leaves_open said a per-name ruling cannot suppress the next SKU of the same shape and recorded 0 occurrences with a watch. Today two further Ben's Original Ready Rice FLAVOUR SKUs and a further Stayfree SKU paged for the first time, so the watch fired exactly as designed and the count is no longer 0.

surface_fix.what: rule the four products that are genuinely a different product, so the sweep stops paging them and the ruling is enforced at publish

items.root_cause: CARRIED FORWARD VERBATIM from plan-2026-09-18.json item 2026-09-18-37ac63: the sweep's alert cannot tell 'no include matches' from 'an exclude refused it', so every product a rule correctly refuses is re-paged as invisible; and the only suppressor it honours is a per-name ruling, which a store defeats by listing the next SKU (4-count after 12-count) and which the -File comma trap can silently turn into a ruling that matches nothing.

root_fix.what: clause 1 (the classifier) and clause 3 (the comma trap) shipped on 2026-09-18 and are demonstrably working today - 14 of 22 findings suppressed. Clause 2, that a per-name ruling cannot cover the next SKU of a shape, is the half still open and is what returned today.
root_fix.exact_change: no change to the classifier or the comma guard: both verified live. Today's change is the four rulings. The shape-scoped ruling that would close clause 2 is NOT invented here - no reviewer has measured what a pattern-keyed known-wrong entry would suppress across 326 existing rulings, and guessing it is exactly the structural change this lane is told not to invent. It is raised as Q1.

items.leaves_open: 8 of today's sweep findings are adjudicated but only 4 are closed: 4 ruled, and 4 real products (feminine-pads x2, maple-syrup x1, onion-soup-mix x1) stay rule-invisible because the gated widening that fixes them was REFUSED by audit-tile-integrity on 2 pre-existing feminine-pads PRICE-DRIFT faults (Sam's Club, Fareway) out of 223 board-wide. Separately, clause 2 of the root cause (a per-name ruling cannot cover the next SKU of a shape) is still open.
items.leaves_open_occurrences: the sweep has paged on 3 days in the 30-day window (2026-09-18 seven findings, 2026-09-19 one, 2026-09-20 eight) and open item 2026-09-19-4f01f6 carries count 3 with today's 8 as its recorded recurrence. The next-SKU class fired 3 times today (two Ben's flavour SKUs, one Stayfree SKU), up from the 0 occurrences 37ac63 recorded.

prevention.what: the emitting check classifies every finding with explain-coverage-gap's own classifier before it pages, so only genuinely rule-invisible products reach a human, and any widening they imply goes through the gated batch rather than a hand edit

open_questions_for_brad.question: known-wrong is keyed on commodity|store|normalised NAME, so every new SKU of an already-adjudicated shape pages again. 37ac63 recorded this at 0 occurrences on 2026-09-18; it fired 3 times today (two Ben's Original Ready Rice flavour SKUs, one Stayfree SKU). Should a ruling be allowed to carry a PATTERN as well as a name? It is a real change to how 326 rulings are enforced and no reviewer has measured what a pattern-keyed entry would suppress, so this lane did not invent it.
open_questions_for_brad.recommendation: measure first: run every existing ruling's stored name against the full corpus as a pattern and report how many extra rows each would suppress, before any schema change.
open_questions_for_brad.answer: Brad 2026-09-25: "Measure first, then decide (Recommended)". Measured the same day: design/MEASURE-known-wrong-pattern-rulings-2026-09-25.md, harness grocery/probe-known-wrong-patterns.ps1, one row per ruling per derivation. Over 333 active rulings and 54,923 captured store and product pairs, a size-count pattern blocks 10 extra products (7 rulings, 0 ruled wrong, 1 published cell), a flavour pattern 12 (9 rulings, 0 ruled wrong, 1 published cell), a first-three-words shape 169 (70 rulings, 10 ruled wrong, 16 published cells). None passes the safety bar written before the run. Brad's ruling B of 2026-09-22 on this question id (queue 2026-09-21-7d64a6: a recurring shape becomes a commodity exclude) stands unchanged; the decision after the measurement is Brad's.
open_questions_for_brad.ruling: Brad 2026-09-25, after design/MEASURE-known-wrong-pattern-rulings-2026-09-25.md: "Keep exact names only, close it (Recommended)". known-wrong rulings stay keyed on the exact normalised product name; no pattern-keyed entry is added, because every pattern derivation measured blocks products nobody ruled wrong (first-three-words: 70 of 333 rulings, 169 extra products, 16 live cells).
